scope: The relation between K1346's scalar phase on the entire nontrivial irreducible principal-series Hilbert fibre and one-parameter subgroups of Spin_0(7,7); not a prohibition on nonuniform subgroup weights after symmetry reduction.

scalar_phase_theorem.representation: pi is K1335's nontrivial irreducible unitary spherical principal series on H_ps=L2(K/M)
scalar_phase_theorem.hypothesis: for X in g, pi(exp(tX))=exp(i q t) I on all H_ps
scalar_phase_theorem.commutator_identity: d pi([X,Y])=[d pi(X),d pi(Y)]=0 for every Y
scalar_phase_theorem.faithfulness_reason: the kernel of a nontrivial Lie-algebra representation of simple g is a proper ideal, hence zero
scalar_phase_theorem.centrality_conclusion: [X,Y]=0 for every Y, so X lies in the zero center of g
scalar_phase_theorem.result: X=0 and q=0; no nontrivial internal one-parameter subgroup acts as one common scalar phase

charge_sector_theorem.candidate: a nonzero fixed-q eigenspace H_q for a noncentral internal U(1) subgroup
charge_sector_theorem.full_G_invariance_test: a nonzero closed G-invariant H_q equals H_ps by irreducibility
charge_sector_theorem.contradiction: if H_q=H_ps then the subgroup acts by one scalar phase on all H_ps, contradicting the scalar-phase theorem for q nonzero
charge_sector_theorem.surviving_scope: a nonzero charge sector may be preserved by the subgroup centralizer or normalizer, not by the full G action

claim_ceiling: K1346's field-wide common phase is not the restriction of the nontrivial Spin_0(7,7) principal-series action. Selecting a nonzero charge eigenspace of an internal subgroup necessarily reduces the preserved internal symmetry. The theorem leaves nonuniform charge decompositions, stabilizer-selected sectors and externally commuting gauge factors open.
